Self-effacing

self-uh-FAY-sing · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Self-effacing is modest and reluctant to draw attention to oneself or one's achievements.

The self-effacing scientist credited her entire lab, not herself, when accepting the award.

Worked Example

Despite writing a bestselling book, the self-effacing author still described herself as 'just someone who got lucky.'

Self-effacing describes a genuine reluctance to accept praise or draw attention to one's own achievements.

How Self-effacing Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

modest

modest: having a moderate view of one's own importance

unassuming

unassuming: not showy or arrogant

Antonyms

boastful

boastful: showing excessive pride in one's achievements

arrogant

arrogant: having an inflated sense of one's own importance

How Strong Is It? — modest → humble → self-effacing

modest vs. self-effacing

modest vs. self-effacing: Modest is the everyday word for downplaying one's achievements; self-effacing goes further, actively avoiding attention or credit.

humble vs. self-effacing

humble vs. self-effacing: Humble carries a similar quiet quality, but self-effacing more specifically emphasizes deflecting praise onto others.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Self-effacing is a compound of 'self' and 'effacing' (from efface, 'to rub out or erase'), literally describing someone who tries to erase their own presence from the spotlight.

Use the root in a new word: deface

Use the root in a new word: deface: Deface comes from the same Latin root facies ('face') buried inside efface, though deface means to spoil the surface of something, quite different from self-effacing's modest retreat from attention.
